title: Selecting many .desktop files on the desktop causes extreme lag on high-resolution screens
line: Dragging a selection rectangle over many desktop icons no longer makes the desktop lag.
explanation: On every pointer move during a rubber band selection, rectangleSelect() called contentItem.childAt() once per grid cell, and childAt() itself maps the point into every child, so the cost grew with the square of the icon count even over empty space. On every selection change, Positioner re-emitted dataChanged without the roles, so each changed delegate re-read all its roles, including the icon, which re-reads the .desktop file and its symlink chain; FolderModel also ran updateActions() (file properties, new-file templates, theme icons) each time. The change looks delegates up with itemAtIndex(), forwards the changed roles through Positioner like its non-positioning path already does, and updates the actions once when the rubber band ends.

commits.message:
containments/desktop: make rubber band selection cheaper

Each pointer move hit-tested all items per cell, and each selection
change reloaded every role of the icons and rebuilt the actions. Find
delegates by index, forward changed roles, update actions at the end.

BUG: 493376

media.caption: Master: plasmashell's main thread spends 2.75 s of a 5.8 s sweep at 2560x1440@144 with 176 icons, 3.23 s even when sweeping empty space
With the fix: 1.15 s across the icons and 0.87 s over empty space for the same sweep

review.text: Solid, well-profiled performance fix addressing three distinct bottlenecks in desktop rubber-band selection: replacing the O(N^2) contentItem.childAt() scan and manual RTL grid math with gridView.itemAtIndex(), forwarding changed roles in Positioner::sourceDataChanged() when custom positioning is enabled (avoiding repeated KFileItem::overlays() symlink/desktop-file I/O), and deferring FolderModel::updateActions() until unpinSelection() when the drag ends. The diff is clean and removes more lines than it adds, passes all folder/positioner/screenmapper autotests, and is backed by clear main-thread CPU measurements and matching selection screenshots.

reviews.text: Solid, well-profiled performance fix addressing three distinct bottlenecks in desktop rubber-band selection: replacing the O(N^2) contentItem.childAt() scan and manual RTL grid math with gridView.itemAtIndex(), forwarding changed roles in Positioner::sourceDataChanged() when custom positioning is enabled (avoiding repeated KFileItem::overlays() symlink/desktop-file I/O), and deferring FolderModel::updateActions() until unpinSelection() when the drag ends. The diff is clean and removes more lines than it adds, passes all folder/positioner/screenmapper autotests, and is backed by clear main-thread CPU measurements and matching selection screenshots.

The three changes are sound and in the right place: itemAtIndex() replaces the O(n^2) childAt() hit-test (and handles RTL without the hand-mirrored math), Positioner now forwards the changed roles like its other path so selection changes no longer re-read icons/overlays, and updateActions() is deferred while the selection is pinned, with pressCanceled() always unpinning. But the evidence only shows main-thread CPU dropping (2.75 -> 1.15 s); the rig's frame counts were about the same before and after (361 vs 385), so it is not shown that the dropped frames the reporter sees are gone. The reporter's lag scales with screen resolution and not with icon size (c29, c34), which points at a render-side cost this patch doesn't touch, and the notes admit that each change still loads/unloads the per-icon highlight Loader.
changes: Show the user-visible lag is gone: frame timing or dropped-frame counts for the same sweep that clearly differ before vs after (e.g. lower resolution, or a GPU-backed session), not just main-thread CPU.

If frames still drop, also address the remaining per-selection-change cost (e.g. keep the PlasmaExtras.Highlight instantiated and toggle visibility/opacity instead of loading/unloading it) and whatever makes the cost scale with resolution.
Otherwise land this commit as CCBUG: 493376 (a solid partial improvement) and keep BUG: for the change that removes the remaining lag.
